Article Title: OFFSIDE | Gianni Infantino: The man who tried to sell football
Article Text:
How FIFA’s most powerful president tried to turn football’s greatest prize into a $20-billion investment vehicle — and finally discovered the limits of his power.

Infantino says ‘nobody’ is trying to sell the World Cup. (AI Cartoon by Nirmalya Dutta.)

The Trojan Horse

polytropos

bandobast

bandobast

bandobast

Infantino’s Trojan horse of privatisation fell flat. (AI cartoon by Nirmalya Dutta)

The fallout

The end of the road?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hello and welcome to a new version of OFFSIDE, a weekly newsletter looking at everything happening in the Beautiful Game.One pivotal moment in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey shows just how far the film departs from Homer’s epic. In the original, Odysseus tells the Cyclops Polyphemus that his name is “Outis”, meaning “Nobody” or “No One”, before he and his men blind him. When the other Cyclopes come to check on Polyphemus, they are told that “Nobody” is attacking him, leaving them with little reason to intervene.Odysseus escapes the cave, yet cannot resist taunting Polyphemus and revealing his true identity. That gives the Cyclops everything he needs to escalate the complaint to his father, Poseidon, god of the sea, who turns the journey home for Odysseus and Co into the ancient Ryanair experience. That version doesn’t exist in Nolan’s movie, which transforms Odysseus from Homer’s polytropos, the “man of many turns” whose cunning is matched by the hubris that angers the gods, into a traumatised veteran who simply wants to return home to his wife.Speaking of hubris that angers the gods, Gianni Infantino, a man who has changed football in every feasible way to improve FIFA’s relationship with Mammon, was at it again after his plan to “sell the World Cup” was leaked.Once caught out, he channelled his inner Odysseus and insisted that “nobody” was selling football.The comparison ends there.Odysseus’ Trojan Horse made it through the gates of Troy. Infantino’s never got past the turnstile, perhaps because this was hardly his first rodeo and, for once, the footballing world decided, to borrow a line from Sir Alex Ferguson, to check under the pasta to see what was under the sauce.So here’s the Homeric story of the modern-day Odysseus, who thought he could get away with it all till the footballing world finally caught on.Much as it describes Homer’s protagonist, the word– a man of many turns – could very well be used to describe the Swiss man from a nondescript village who had become the most powerful man in football’s history, one whom Donald Trump referred to as the “King of Soccer”. Perhaps he felt even the Fates were intervening on his behalf when the winds blew Donald Trump back into the White House to ensure that the FIFA World Cup in America would be everything his heart desired.One particular anecdote illustrates how Infantino came to view himself amid the pantheon of global soccer stars and movers and shakers in international politics.In India, there’s a term calledthat translates to “arrangement”, “management” or “organisation”. It refers to the deployment of police, security protocols and logistical arrangements when a VIP is in town and is seen by many as a social marker of power. According to a report by Martyn Ziegler in The Sunday Times, FIFA requested a similarfor him in Canada, seeking the same transport privileges reserved for the US president. The request was declined by Canadian police.Therequest was just the tip of the iceberg. Infantino even has a personal photographer as his “Instagram husband”, someone whose job is to click every moment of his life. He engraved his name twice on the Club World Cup trophy and cast himself as a global peacemaker who brought two “warring nations” to the World Cup.All that is evident in the handprint he has left on the global game.During his tenure, Infantino has managed to expand the World Cup from 32 teams to 48 teams, revamped the Club World Cup into a mini-World Cup with 32 teams, broken football’s long-standing traditions to force through hydration breaks and a half-time show, introduced dynamic pricing for FIFA matches and got players’ bans rescinded, including Ronaldo’s and Folarin Balogun’s. He gave Trump a FIFA Peace Prize when the Nobel Committee wouldn’t give him one and engineered the 2030 tournament by ensuring that it would be played across Europe, Africa and South America to ensure that Saudi Arabia got it in 2034.Earlier, he also tried to push through a secretive $25-billion, 12-year proposal involving SoftBank that envisaged an expanded Club World Cup and a global Nations League culminating in a “Final 8” tournament. That fell through, and he even tried to hold the World Cup every two years instead of four.While neither went forward, both moves emboldened Infantino to think that perhaps his FFE Trojan Horse would go through unchecked.The FFE plan, which sounds rather innocuous, like corporate CSR efforts, was very simple: create a different entity called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a subsidiary dealing with FIFA’s main mission: improving its relationship with the only god that matters, Mammon.The new company would take care of everything financial: broadcasting rights, sponsorship, ticketing and operational delivery. JPMorgan valued this company at $20 billion, and FIFA would sell a $4.2-billion stake to outside investors while retaining 80%. The pitch was that FIFA was “undermonetised”, with annual revenue of $3.6 billion compared with the NFL’s $21.2 billion, MLB’s $13.1 billion and the NBA’s $12.5 billion.The idea was to grow FIFA’s event portfolio, a hard ask given that the NFL and others are annual franchise leagues, while FIFA is a governing body whose main income is concentrated around periodic tournaments. Infantino hoped to pull this off by promising FIFA’s 211 members $20 million during the next four-year cycle, double the $10 million they were due to receive, with one caveat: they had to come on board as soon as possible.Infantino envisaged himself as the chair of this company once he retired from FIFA in 2030, with a basic annual salary of $30 million, even joking that by 2031 “we can make serious money”. When asked whether his current $6 million annual salary wasn’t enough, he replied: “No, I’m talking a serious amount.”For Odysseus, the fallout started when he announced his name to the Cyclops Polyphemus, earning Poseidon’s wrath. For Infantino, the fallout began on July 28, when The Times (UK) and the Financial Times, in a moment reminiscent of Leibniz and Newton’s independent development of calculus, laid bare Infantino’s plan to sell stakes to a private company. The proposed investor group would be led by Josh Kushner, brother of Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s son-in-law. FIFA was at pains to point out that Josh, unlike his brother, was a registered Democrat who had donated to Obama’s campaign and attended Taylor Swift’s wedding. According to Forbes, he has a net worth of $5.2 billion. In the finance world in particular, Josh is the one who matters and is known for his financial acumen, including a major investment in Instagram that doubled in value in a few days.The angriest remonstrations – enough to make Gertrude wonder whether UEFA “doth protest too much” – came from Europe, which said the “soul and governance of football are not assets to be sold”, a worldview seldom expressed when teams of sportswashing nations break UEFA’s financial fair play regulations.Things came to a head when all 55 UEFA nations agreed to boycott the men’s and women’s World Cups. CONCACAF opposed FFE over the lack of due process, while the AFC called the plan “totally unacceptable”.Senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned, calling it a “bad deal for football”, while FIFA’s chief operating officer (COO), Kevin Lamour, claimed that they had been “deceived” and that it was the “project of one person”.Soon, the screws started turning for Infantino, with UEFA saying FIFA’s leadership had lost “UEFA’s confidence”. CONCACAF said the plan was a “symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first”. The English FA said it would send a letter to Infantino withdrawing its support for his re-election. Other European nations are expected to follow suit. In fact, UEFA has the power to trigger an Extraordinary FIFA Congress without help from any other confederation. The rules require 20% of FIFA’s 211 members, or 43 associations, and UEFA has 55. Calls for his resignation are also gaining traction. UK PM Andy Burnham, freshly burnished in the role after Starmer’s resignation, has called for him to step down. LaLiga president Javier Tebas has followed suit.Of course, Infantino retains strong support from CAF, CONMEBOL and smaller Asian, Caribbean and Pacific federations that rely heavily on FIFA’s development funding.Perhaps Infantino’s time is up and his fate seems sealed, like that of a tragic hero from the Russian rather than the Greek tradition. The alacrity with which folks who benefited from Infantino turning football into a capitalist behemoth have suddenly discovered hitherto unseen principles is very reminiscent of an old Russian short story by Anton Chekhov titled The Confession. Its protagonist is a cashier who suddenly becomes the cat that got the cream when he gets a minor promotion and finds himself courted, respected and invited by everyone.Then, as he gets mired in scandal, he is quickly dropped. The patrons disappear, and his family turns scornful. The court is only loyal as long as the gifts keep coming; as soon as the gifts become liabilities, that loyalty develops a conscience.Infantino hasn’t been banished from Zurich yet, but he is getting the treatment that would have befallen Odysseus if the Trojan Horse had been burned instead of taken inside the walled city. For the last decade, Infantino has been treated as soccer’s God, but over the past few extraordinary days, he has come to be treated as the man who tarnished world football, even as everyone enjoys the fruits of his spoils. One wouldn’t be surprised if Infantino suddenly felt like quoting Chekhov’s cashier: “My dear ladies and gentlemen, I got caught, or to state it more fully: yesterday I was respected and honoured on all sides; today I am a scoundrel and a thief. .. Cry out, now, banish me, write editorials, and throw stones, please—not everyone.”
Article Summary: Gianni Infantino tried to turn the World Cup into a $20-billion investment vehicle. The FIFA president has become the most powerful man in football’s history. He has changed football in every feasible way to improve FIFA's relationship with Mammon. FIFA has also introduced a half-time pricing dynamic, breaking long-standing traditions.

Article Title: World Cup rights gamble backfires: Wales withdraw support for Infantino's FIFA re-election bid
Article Text:
Gianni Infantino

Wales have become the first home nation to withdraw support for Gianni Infantino's bid to remain FIFA president after his proposal to sell a stake in the commercial rights of the World Cup and other FIFA competitions was abandoned.The Football Association of Wales (FAW) said it will no longer back Infantino's re-election campaign for the 2027-2031 term, following concerns over the failed investment plan.FIFA had proposed raising up to $4.2 billion by selling about a 20% stake in a new entity that would manage the commercial rights of competitions including the World Cup. However, the proposal was withdrawn on Friday after facing strong opposition from stakeholders.With the plan shelved, attention has shifted to the possible impact on Infantino's chances of securing another term as FIFA president.The proposal had also triggered strong criticism from across world football. UEFA had warned it could boycott FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, if the plan went ahead.On Saturday, both UEFA and Concacaf, the governing body for football in North, Central America and the Caribbean, issued statements criticising FIFA's leadership following Infantino's decision to withdraw the proposal.The FAW is among the first national football associations to publicly oppose Infantino's re-election.In a statement, the FAW confirmed "its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Gianni Infantino for re-election as Fifa president for the 2027-2031 term".Explaining its decision, the Welsh governing body said:"The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football."Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept."
Article Summary: Wales withdraw support for Gianni Infantino's bid to remain FIFA president. Football Association of Wales said it will no longer back his re-election campaign. FIFA had proposed raising up to $4.2 billion by selling a 20% stake in a new entity.

Article Title: 'Vozinha! Vozinha!': FIFA World Cup breakout star gets hero's welcome in Chile after three delays
Article Text:
Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha arrives at the airport ahead of a move to Colo-Colo in Santiago, Chile. (AP Photo)

Three delays before dream move finally became reality



World Cup hero earns special jersey exception

One of the biggest breakout stars of the 2026 FIFA World Cup has finally arrived in Chile — and the reception was nothing short of extraordinary.Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, whose remarkable performances at the World Cup captured the imagination of football fans across the globe, landed in Santiago on Sunday to complete his move to Chilean giants Colo Colo after his arrival was delayed on three separate occasions.Hundreds of jubilant supporters gathered at Santiago's airport with flags, banners, drums and chants, turning the veteran goalkeeper's arrival into a celebration usually reserved for legends. Videos of the emotional welcome quickly spread across social media, underlining the popularity Vozinha has earned since his unforgettable World Cup campaign."I’m very happy to be here. And I want to thank the fans for the patience they’ve shown while waiting for me," the 40-year-old told reporters shortly after landing. "See you at the Monumental Stadium."Colo Colo, Chile's most successful football club, announced the signing of Josimar Évora Dias — better known worldwide as Vozinha — on July 24.However, what was expected to be a straightforward transfer soon became a complicated saga.Documentation issues and personal matters delayed the goalkeeper's arrival three different times, raising concerns among supporters eagerly waiting to welcome their new signing.The uncertainty finally ended on Sunday evening when Vozinha landed in Santiago at 8:35 p.m. local time to a rousing reception from hundreds of Colo Colo fans.The veteran is scheduled to undergo medical examinations before signing an initial six-month contract with an option to extend it by another year. He is expected to begin training with his new teammates on Tuesday before being officially unveiled by the club.Vozinha's move has already prompted an unprecedented rule change in Chilean football.The Chilean Football Federation unanimously voted to amend its regulations and allow the goalkeeper to wear "Vozinha" on the back of his jersey instead of his surname.Under previous league rules, players were required to display only their family names on their shirts.The exception reflects the global recognition attached to the nickname that became synonymous with Cape Verde's historic World Cup journey.Vozinha — whose nickname means "grandma" in Portuguese — became one of the tournament's most celebrated players after helping Cape Verde make history on their World Cup debut.At 40, he became the oldest player to feature in a nation's first-ever World Cup match and earned worldwide admiration with a string of spectacular saves against Spain, Uruguay and Argentina. His heroic display against eventual champions Spain, where he kept them scoreless, transformed him into one of the faces of the tournament.His popularity exploded during the competition. Before the World Cup, Vozinha had fewer than 50,000 Instagram followers. By the end of the tournament, that figure had soared beyond 29.5 million.For Colo Colo supporters, the excitement extends well beyond social media fame.Fans hope the experienced goalkeeper can inspire the Chilean league leaders to another domestic title before leading their challenge in next season's Copa Libertadores.
Article Summary: Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha lands in Chile to complete move to Colo Colo. The 40-year-old became one of the biggest breakout stars of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. His arrival at Santiago's airport was met by hundreds of jubilant fans.

Article Title: Raengdai FC: A football fairytale from conflict-hit Manipur
Article Text:
Image credit: TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Eduardo Galeano, in his sports writing masterpiece, “Football in Sun and Shadow”, writes that “a reporter once asked German theologian Dorothee Sölle, ‘How would you explain happiness to a child?’ ‘I wouldn’t explain it,’ she answered. ‘I’d toss him a ball and let him play.”The game of football holds the power to elicit joy not just in the one with the ball at his feet but also in the others cherishing its magic from off the field, sometimes even when the lives on both ends of the field are caught in an unfortunate strife.That’s the reality of the people of Noney in Manipur — around 63 km west of capital Imphal — and home to Zeliangrong community, comprising Zeme, Liangmai, Rongmei, and Inpui tribes.After “insurgency”, “militant attacks”, “killings” and “curfews” dominated most headlines from the region in the last couple of years, football has brought them in the limelight in the form of Raengdai FC – the club from the region that has been ascending the Indian football ladder with consistency and swiftness.The latest achievement for the four-year-old club was their historic debut in Durand Cup with a 1-0 victory over last season’s quarterfinalists, Indian Navy.“There was naturally a bit of nervousness because of their quality and experience, but that never stopped us from believing in ourselves,” said Raengdai head coach Birbal Singh Kshetrimayum.Raengdai won the Manipur Premier League in 2024 and got the chance to play in I-League 3 during 2024-25 — a chance that they grabbed with both hands. They then won the AIFF competition upon debut to earn promotion into I-League 2 for the upcoming season.It’s the story of a journey that began on Nov 6, 2022, at Centre Point Food Plaza in Imphal when football enthusiasts in the community got together to find a pathway for the youngsters, who they believed had talent aplenty, to make a career in football.“When we founded FC Raengdai, our vision was simple — to create a proper grassroots football pathway for Zeliangrong community. We knew there was plenty of talent in our villages and towns, but many young players lacked the opportunity and platform to showcase their abilities,” says club general secretary Napoleon Rongmei. “FC Raengdai was created to change that.”And it did change the football landscape in the area. It showed the footballing talents the path towards “building a brighter future for the next generation of footballers”.It was at this juncture, on May 3, 2023, that the conflict began in Manipur. With sports across the region coming to a halt, it had its impact even on the newly formed club, too. There was no football activity for two years and it eventually resumed in 2024.But having their training facilities in Imphal helped, as the players could be away from the friction of the conflict and focus on their game.With players not just from Zeliangrong community but from all over the state, Raengdai built a squad, competed and won the 33rd NM Gupta Football Tournament 2024 in Silchar.And when the call came from MPL — the premier club competition in the state — to participate, Raengdai etched their name in Manipur football by emerging champions of the 2nd edition in 2025.Striker Tingkaochun Gangmei, who began playing football in the local grounds, asserts: “Joining FC Raengdai in 2023 was a turning point in my career. It is my first senior club, and together we competed in the Manipur Premier League before earning promotion through I-League 3. Now, to represent FC Raengdai in our first-ever Durand Cup is something I never imagined as a child playing in Khoupum Valley. It makes me proud not only for myself but also for my family and everyone back home. ”Noney also shares Manipur’s higher literacy rate, ranking 10th nationally, and parents in the area didn’t think of football as a better option compared to studies, for their children.“In a typical Rongmei Naga family, football is rarely considered a viable career option. Thinking outside the box and letting my son become a footballer was one of the hardest decisions my family ever made,” said midfielder Gaisuangmei Kamei’s father.“Initially, as parents, we wanted him to pursue formal education at school. However, we ultimately chose to respect his choice. Looking back now, I realize that it was not a bad decision at all.”It was those collective decisions that aided the rise of the community-funded club that, despite financial struggles, is becoming a growing name in Indian football scene.On Monday, they will be at Khuman Lampak Stadium — expected to be packed with fans — for their second match of Durand Cup, incidentally a Manipur derby against TRAU FC.“In a match like this, the crowd can create extra pressure, but that’s part of football. I have told the players that they must be mentally strong, physically ready and enjoy the occasion rather than be overwhelmed by it,” said Kshetrimayum.As for the community back home and in the stands, they will look to Raengdai to once again make the headlines for its footballing merit.
Article Summary: FC Raengdai is a Manipur-based football club. The club was formed in 2022 to help local players make a career in the game. They won the Manipur Premier League in 2024 and got the chance to play in I-League 3 during 2024-25.

Article Title: Gianni Infantino was to earn $30m base salary if FIFA's plan to sell World Cup stakes went through: reports
Article Text:
FILE - FIFA President Gianni Infantino follows an international friendly soccer match between Iran and Costa Rica, in Antalya, southern Turkey, Tuesday, March 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Riza Ozel, File)

Reports claim Infantino was set for $30 million salary

FFE proposal sparked unprecedented backlash

UEFA says confidence in FIFA leadership has been lost

FIFA disputes reports and explains withdrawal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fallout continues despite proposal being shelved

Gianni Infantino was reportedly in line to receive a $30 million annual base salary under FIFA's now-abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project, according to reports, adding another controversial dimension to a proposal that ultimately collapsed following widespread opposition from football's governing bodies and member associations.The reported remuneration plan surfaced just days after FIFA officially withdrew the proposal to create FFE, a new commercial entity that would have overseen FIFA's competitions while allowing private investors to acquire a minority stake in its commercial rights. The project was abandoned after strong resistance from UEFA, Concacaf, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), national football associations and senior figures within FIFA itself.According to The Times, cited by multiple British publications, the long-term vision for the FFE project would have seen Infantino assume the role of chief executive or commissioner of the new commercial entity.In that position, the FIFA president was reportedly set to receive an annual base salary of approximately $30 million, excluding any additional performance-related bonuses or incentives.The reports suggested the proposal extended beyond attracting private investment into FIFA competitions and envisaged a new executive structure under the commercial arm.FIFA, however, has rejected suggestions that such a remuneration package or executive arrangement was ever formally proposed.The controversy centred on FIFA's proposal to establish FIFA Forward Enterprise, which would have allowed outside investors to purchase a minority stake in the commercial rights of competitions including the FIFA World Cup.As previously reported, the proposal triggered fierce opposition across world football.UEFA's 55 member associations unanimously rejected the plan and warned they would boycott FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, if the proposal proceeded. Concacaf and the AFC subsequently joined UEFA in publicly opposing the project, while FIFA President Gianni Infantino's senior adviser, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned in protest, describing the proposal as "a bad deal for football."Faced with mounting resistance, FIFA eventually withdrew the proposal before any vote took place.Although FIFA abandoned the project, UEFA insisted the decision alone was not enough to restore confidence.In a strongly worded statement, the European governing body said:"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account."UEFA added:"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental."The statement concluded with perhaps its strongest criticism:"No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family."The English Football Association also backed UEFA's position, saying:"We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."Concacaf likewise called for "a comprehensive reckoning" of Infantino's presidency, describing the controversy as "a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first."Throughout the controversy, FIFA maintained that FFE remained only a consultation proposal rather than a finalised commercial structure.After confirming the project would no longer proceed, Infantino said:"The FFE project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed."He added:"And, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders."Explaining the decision to abandon the proposal, Infantino continued:"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place."He concluded:"Our purpose has always been, and will always be, to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that most need our support."While FIFA's decision brought an end to the FFE project, questions surrounding its origins and governance continue to reverberate across world football.The reported $30 million salary plan, although disputed by FIFA, has added fresh scrutiny to a proposal that had already prompted boycott threats, public resignations and widespread criticism from confederations representing more than half of FIFA's 211 member associations.Even with the proposal now withdrawn, the debate over FIFA's governance and leadership shows little sign of ending as stakeholders continue to examine how the controversial project advanced as far as it did before ultimately being abandoned.
Article Summary: Reports claim Infantino was set for $30 million salary. FIFA disputes reports and explains withdrawal of proposal. UEFA says confidence in FIFA leadership has been lost. Concacaf calls for a "comprehensive reckoning" of the FIFA president.

Article Title: “I'm not as good a dad to my kids that my dad’s been to me": How a quietly emotional Tom Brady admitted his children deserved more than the version of himself he gave them
Article Text:
Tom Brady cried talking about his father and fatherhood (Getty Images)

What did Tom Brady say about his father and fatherhood?

Why did Tom Brady say there is a 'torment' he doesn't wish upon his children?

Tom Brady won seven Super Bowls. He outlasted generations of quarterbacks, rewrote NFL records, and made winning look almost boring. But in a candid, tearful moment on ESPN's docuseries *Man in the Arena*, the greatest quarterback in football history said something no trophy can fix. He looked at the camera, thought about his three children, and admitted that the father he has been to them simply does not measure up to the father who raised him. Coming from a man who almost never loses, that hit differently.Tom Brady spoke his heart out. Speaking about his father, Tom Brady Sr., he said: "When I think about being a dad, I think of him. I know I'm not as good a dad to my kids that my dad's been to me. I use him as my example of how to keep a family together and to care, to support, and how to love."That is a remarkable thing for anyone to say publicly. For Brady, a man carefully guarded in interviews, it was almost startling. His father showed up for everything. Every game, every doubt, every moment that needed a steady hand. Brady grew up with that kind of unconditional presence and knows exactly what it looks like. Which is precisely why he feels the gap.Brady is a father to three children. He shares Benjamin and Vivian with ex-wife Gisele Bundchen, and has an older son, Jack, with former girlfriend Bridget Moynahan.By any measure, his children have grown up in extraordinary circumstances. But Brady himself seemed to be measuring something harder to quantify than money or opportunity."I want them to be respectful of people. I want them to be kind," he said. "I think maybe what I'd wish for my children is to find something they love to do like I have. But I think I've taken things to an extreme, too."This is where the conversation got genuinely uncomfortable, in the best way. Tom Brady, who has spent decades building one of the most obsessive athletic careers in sports history, openly questioned whether that obsession was something worth passing down."There are imbalances in my life," he said. "I hope they don't take things as far as I've taken them."He followed that with something even more pointed: "I want them to experience great success in whatever they do. But there's a torment about me that I don't wish upon them."That word, torment, is doing a lot of work. Brady was not talking about pressure or sacrifice in the abstract. He was describing something internal, a relentless drive that served him brilliantly on the field but clearly cost him something at home. Six months before this moment, he had called being a working father "difficult to reconcile," admitting he did not want to miss his children's milestones but often did.Brady briefly retired in February before reversing course within weeks, saying his place was still on the field. The decision was personal, but it also fed directly into this guilt. He knew what he was choosing each time he chose football. He just could not stop choosing it.What makes this resurfaced moment so striking is not the vulnerability, though that is rare enough from Brady. It is the honesty about a trade-off most elite athletes never actually name out loud. Being the best at something, truly the best, can leave marks on the people who love you. Brady knows that. He lives with it. And in that one episode of a documentary, he said so.
Article Summary: Tom Brady spoke about his father, Tom Brady Sr., on ESPN's *Man in the Arena. Brady: "When I think about being a dad, I think of him. I know I'm not as good a dad to my kids that my dad's been to me"
